headline: Webb telescope reveals a deadline for planet birth
standfirst: New data shows forming planets are in a high-stakes race against time.

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: The James Webb Space Telescope studied 72 young stars and found that forming planets is a race.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: Astronomers used the telescope to observe these sun-like stars to see how they build planets.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: It suggests the window of time for planets to form around stars is much tighter than we thought.

steps.label: What to watch
steps.text: Future telescope observations will clarify just how quickly these worlds must come together.

caption:
The James Webb Space Telescope is showing astronomers that planet formation is a race against time.

By observing 72 young stars, researchers have gained a better understanding of how early solar systems develop. This discovery changes our view of how quickly planets must form before their environment changes.

Does it surprise you that the universe has such strict time limits for creating new planets?
